You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e0f3b803d74277677697bdf5b5e4c28766cfbc93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2010 14:21:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>
---
 arch/um/os-Linux/time.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
index dec5678fc17..6e3359d6a83 100644
--- a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
+++ b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ static inline long long timeval_to_ns(const struct timeval *tv)
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was a type mismatch in the variable used to store the remaining time in the `disable_timer` function. The original code declared `remain` as an `int`, while the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This mismatch led to incorrect calculations and ultimately caused the timer to freeze when using the CONFIG_NO_HZ configuration in the UML (User Mode Linux) environment. The fix involved changing the type of `remain` from `int` to `long long` to ensure proper handling of the timer values.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was a type mismatch in the variable used to store the remaining time in the `disable_timer` function. The original code declared `remain` as an `int`, while the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This mismatch led to incorrect calculations and ultimately caused the timer to freeze when using the CONFIG_NO_HZ configuration in the UML (User Mode Linux) environment. The fix involved changing the type of `remain` from `int` to `long long` to ensure proper handling of the timer values.
